notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) HTTP-first succeeded throughout - no browser wall encountered. robots.txt checked first (no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web disallow; standard Shopify robots.txt disallowing /cart,/checkout,/search etc, irrelevant to /collections/*). Fetched via curl/requests with a browser User-Agent. TREE: Site is a large general Shopify home-goods retailer (Francfranc) with a footer 'category list' (nav.footer__category_nav ul.tree-menu, classes first-level/second-level/third-level) that is the authoritative full 3-level category tree, verified via a Playwright headless render (playwright + chromium) since it is JS-rendered; cross-checked against the header mega-menu (c-header-menu-desktop) which matched. Union of that tree plus the header hover flyout for Curtains supplied the deeper ready-made/made-to-order curtain variants not present in the footer tree. Confirmed each collection handle resolves to a live Shopify collection (id present in the site's own /collections.json across 13 pages, 3081 total collections; every handle used here resolved). QTY: Shopify's /collections.json 'products_count' field is confirmed inflated on this store (e.g. handle 'mat' reports 173 there vs the real 44 shown on-page) so it was NOT used, per project rule (products_count unreliable). Instead, discovered the store's own client-side search/filter API (p006.francfranc.com/store-search/products, a Searchanise-style app) via Playwright network capture on a sample collection page; its 'total_count' field exactly matched the rendered on-page '検索結果 N 件' (search result N items) text for that page (44=44), so it was used as the authoritative qty source for every leaf, queried directly via HTTP with page=1&limit=1 (tier a, no Playwright needed per-row). 10 leaves returned qty=0 (bathrobe, bedspread, clothes_rack, file_box, flameproof_curtain [ready-made], magazine_rack_box, mirror_curtain [ready-made], napkin, style_curtain, toilet_storage); toilet_storage was independently spot-checked by re-querying its collection_id directly, confirming a genuine zero-product listing page, recorded as qty=0 per rule (valid category, confirmed zero, not assumed). EXCLUDED: All Furniture (sofa/chair/table/bed/wardrobe/TV stand/cabinet/bookshelf/shoe & coat racks etc), Lighting, Appliances, Fragrance/candles/vases/frames/clocks/mirrors/objects (Decorative Home Accessories), Kitchen & Dining tableware/cookware/glassware/food-storage-container-labelled-but-actually-bottle-lunchbox-pitcher items, Bath/beauty non-textile items (dispenser, body brush/towel combo, hair band, handkerchief - personal accessory not home textile), cleaning/laundry hardware (hangers, clothespins, deodorant, carpet cleaner), Fashion goods (bags, shoes, accessories, roomwear, rain gear, pouches, stationery, toys, CD/books), Outdoor/travel goods, curtain hardware (hooks/runners/hanger clips), and duplicate cross-listed items that the site itself places under its Furniture nav (TV stand/cabinet group 'living_storage', dining/kitchen storage furniture group 'dining_kitchen_storage' except the plain 'kitchen_strage' leaf, bedroom storage furniture group 'bedroom_storage', SOHO office desk/chair/coat-hanger/mirror) per the Furniture-boundary rule (site places these under Furniture primarily; kept out of Storage to avoid duplicate/incorrect rows). The generic '保存容器' (storage container) Kitchen group was excluded from Storage because its only children are bottle/water-bottle, bento/lunch box and pitcher - personal drinkware/food-carry items, not home organization containers. 'Cushion inserts/nude' (fabric cushion filling, 3 leaves) kept in Textile at LOW confidence since the site itself files them under the Fabric nav but they are technically an unstuffed filling component. 'Umbrella stands', 'Baskets', and 'Clothes Racks' kept in Storage at MEDIUM confidence (holding/organizing function, but not explicitly named in storage.md's example lists). No screenshots or LLM page reads were used; all data is deterministic HTTP/JSON.
